title: First USGS generic aftershock forecasts show no clear mean timing error on days 1-30, but four of eight active sequences reject the issued time curve
abstract: We tested recorded aftershock times for 192 first-issued USGS generic forecasts, after fixing each sequence total to remove productivity uncertainty. At thresholds at or above stated catalog completeness, 335 aftershock records entered sequence windows on days 1-30. Of these, 168 were on days 7-30 against 157.09 expected from the issued Omori curves. The observed to expected ratio was 1.069, with a 95% cluster bootstrap interval of 0.894-1.384. There was no clear average timing error. Exploratory conditional uniform-time tests rejected the issued curve for four of eight sequences with at least five events after Holm correction. A change in the decay exponent removed three rejections. Puerto Rico in 2020 still rejected all exponents from 0 to 3 with its issued early-time parameter held fixed, in a conservative composite-model test (adjusted p=0.0391). That result did not persist at a higher magnitude threshold. Productivity changes alone cannot repair every time-distribution error in this snapshot. The tests do not identify secondary triggering as the cause. This is a reanalysis of one catalog snapshot, with many zero-count sequences and few large sequences.
